what_the_old_gate_measured.note: G06 admits width eight only when concurrent paired-cell active dispatch is at most 1.35x the width-1 baseline, under a 150 s scaled dispatch budget (full 1800 s phase / 12). Memory, pageouts, transport validity, semantic validity, parity, and isolation are also required; with the real tool-bearing arms they all passed.

formal_g06_refusal.attempt_2: G06 2x rep 2: per_cell_slowdown_ratio=1.362757 exceeds sealed max 1.35

why_the_measurement_is_real: Unmodified frozen G06 contract; widths 1/2/4/6/8 x 3 repetitions.
Real production arms (candidate flat_exact_associative_monolith; control append_only_history_retrieval).
All objects transport-valid and semantically valid at every width.
Zero pageouts; peak resident memory well below the 85 GiB ceiling.
Width-8 max slowdown 4.392411013227944 is a measured concurrent-dispatch fact, not a modeling artifact.
why_it_is_not_load_bearing_for_odyssey_c: Odyssey scores phases of 1800 s and microcycles of 7200 s. Capacity means finishing work before those deadlines, not matching single-cell generation latency under concurrent GPU sharing.

At width 8, active dispatch was on the order of ~57 s inside an 1800 s phase (~31x deadline headroom). The 4.39x slowdown relative to width 1 does not imply missed phase, microcycle, event, or checkpoint deadlines.
Exact simultaneous token generation is not a treatment variable in the claim boundary: the candidate/control treatment is developmental memory, not concurrency latency.
Tools add ~0.39% of a phase and are CPU-bound; measured GPU idle was 6.58 s of a 6.74 s tool window, so tool work does not contend with model generation for the GPU.
preservation_rule: This record and the referenced WIDTH_CALIBRATION receipt must remain intact. Never hide the 4.39x. G06 and _validate_g06 remain historical evidence; G06-DC is a separate scientific successor gate.
